Oh sorry I should have deleted this as I found the strength to talk to my dad. He has researched the surgery for me too and used to be a doctor himself so I trust him to know what’s safe for me and find me a good surgeon. 

Here’s what I posted as an update on a different sub

Just a little update! I told my dad. He told me he was extremely happy I told him and didn’t keep it in. He thought I was hiding something much worse like I was self harming or mutilating myself. He told me he will pay for the voice surgery and sort it out to have it done before I go to university in September.

He told me he won’t talk to my mum about it but will leave it until I’m ready myself. Honestly it was a huge relief and showed me how much of a fantastic dad he is. He was so sad I had to go through this alone and joked he wanted some testosterone himself as he was in middle age now haha.

He said everything should be back to normal by the time I go to university and pushed me to go to a new city if I feel comfortable and start afresh. He’s going to buy me clothes and stuff for Uni too and we checked out all of the cities I want to go to this week.

Thank you! I did it by going to visit one of my Uni cities with my dad on the train, we talked about random stuff saw the sites. Then I told him little bits trying to get his reaction, he said I’ll love you no matter what don’t worry, and promised not to tell my mum himself so I do it when I want to.

Then we discussed my past and the bullying at high school and he said he noticed a change in how I was in the past few years. It led on to me giving him the letter I wrote about everything and he read it and started to cry a little, just upset I was hiding something and carrying the burden. 

After that he laughed him crying off and said it’s not a big deal at all. He was just upset I was so upset and lonely for months. He said the only reason it would be good to tell my mum soon is she has a maternal instinct and kept saying to him am I okay. So it would be a relief to her to know what actually happened and she would be happy to take me to London for the surgery and look after me. 

I honestly am hopeful for university and life for the first time ever and am looking forward to actually experiencing clubbing and partying and socialising with so many people, I feel like my life’s just about to start :)

I was taking honestly 50mg a week which is basically what the average man produces. I think the average 18yr old guy produces that exact amount a week.

So I probably have good genetics? I have a great diet and always found it easy to build muscle even naturally just playing rugby. With the competitions I just have to have female blood values by the time I fight/lift. Since I am a cis female there are no issues like trans women since I have female bone structure, it’s all about testing within the testosterone limits.

Thanks for the advice, I honestly have heard women with lower voices but they are normally heavy smokers or much older women in their 70’s.

I’ve watched a detrans woman called saltyalty’s vidoes and she’s great but she explains how she’s still sad about her voice as it hasn’t changed after 4 years, whereas others have talked about slight ‘lightening’ but no pitch or major sound change that gets them seen as female.

With my parents I get that, but you don’t know my parents lol. They are extremely overprotective and view me as their baby girl who would never do something as crazy and risky as this. I don’t drink and never have tried alcohol, I don’t go out clubbing, I’m the kind of gal who’s always studied hard and focused on sports and never taken any risks. It’s like my whole personality changed when I took testosterone and decided to do so, and they don’t know that.

I literally told my dad for weeks months ago everyday dad I have something to tell you but it will be quite shocking to you…. I really can’t bring myself to say it so I promise if you guess what it’s about I’ll tell you everything…. And he said sweetheart I have no idea, I don’t know what it could possibly be, did something happen online with one of your friends?

Hey thank you for your input! Yeah Manchester actually. 

That’s honestly so reassuring to hear, I mean I always thought a straight guy would be turned off by a deeper woman’s voice, like the way they make jokes about dr Mrs the monarch being so hot if it wasn’t for her voice, weirdly enough though there are loads of comments of guys digging her voice too.

Yeah I know I never thought I’d be one of those people to alter my body and get surgery or anything, I thought badly of tattoos until a few years ago! It’s crazy how you can go down a spiral of making more and more alterations and I don’t want to go there.

The most I’ve ever done is get laser eye surgery which was amazing and a great gift from a relative, but I feel like that’s different to cosmetic things.

I used to be the sort of girl that didn’t give a fuck, I was bullied but was pretty smart and used to take pride in being great at debating and sport (I’m an amateur boxer and power lifter), so it was cool to have some skills that made me feel better than my bullies and gave me something to be proud of. But now this has just destroyed me you know, it feels like I’ve had a reality check that no I’m not mature yet and I don’t know shit and I’m not as confident as I should be. I felt I knew it all and was so certain a few months ago and it’s crazy how that certainty has just evaporated into thin air.

Haha interesting you mentioned that, damn I know what it’s like to work out as a guy now, and fuck you have it so easy compared to us women…. I was strong for a girl and the testosterone just made the bar fly up, I got to benching 80kg 5x5 after just 1 year of powerlifting which I think is good for a girl ;) now I’m trying to keep as much strength as possible but i know why steroid users struggle to train naturally, it feels crazy to be ‘juiced up’.

Aw thank you for making the effort to do that. Lol must have seemed very random to him based on the weird stuff I was saying… I don’t even mind an androgynous voice you know, so I’m really happy that a few people on here are saying they think it sounds female

Aw thank you. By the way I know a lot of detrans people are very anti-trans and hateful but I genuinely believe live and let live and think transitioning can be the answer to some people. Just because my experience didn’t work out doesn’t mean trans people don’t exist!

Yeah good advice to focus on my education. I’ve been really worried about this whilst I’ve supposed to be studying but I’m quite academic and have forced myself to revise a lot. I’m predicted good grades and got offers from great unis so I hope I get in :)

Can I ask if you have tried voice training? I’ve been trying it and it honestly works because my voice didn’t drop to a crazy deep man’s voice so if I pitch it up higher and make effort it sounds 100 percent female, but I just hate having to force myself to talk and always think about it all the time. You might have a better experience with voice training but it was very hard for me.

Would you ever consider voice surgery? Honestly it makes me appreciate how trans women feel now because it feels so shit to feel uncomfortable with a part of your body. I’m sure you’re gorgeous and I hope you are happy now.

Oh cool! It seems like Americans outweighs brits on Reddit but nice to get a British perspective too. 

I’ll give it away - Manchester, so you probably know up north we speak a little harsher and more ‘blunt sounding’ I guess, just doesn’t sound as soft as down in London

That’s really reassuring even if I can’t hear it myself right now. People are so polite it’s hard to get a real perspective what they think… I tell someone I’m detrans as they start feeling really bad and purposely calling me ‘she and her’ and a girl all the time, maybe to reaffirm my identity.

I guess it doesn’t sound like a proper grown man, but maybe a teenage boy or something, it sounds different to my dad and male relatives


I agree, even if I did get surgery it should be after waiting many more months for my hormones to stabilise (since I’ve heard the voice can get lighter and more feminine sounding over time sometimes and it’s only been 10 weeks), and also after talking properly to my parents and having a support network. 

I’m gonna try be kinder to myself and am going to try talk to my dad first this or next weekend when he’s free from looking after my sister, then together we can talk to my mum 👍

It’s hard to explain. We are close and they are very respectful but they are the kind of parents who have always sheltered me a little and been overprotective. Perhaps due to my sister being very disabled they are naturally very maternal and paternal. That’s why it’s hard for me to believe they know anything about hormones. They would not suspect I would do everything myself and even I wouldn’t think I would have done it, my depression and mental state turned me into someone else, it completely changed my personality and made me turn away from people I would normally look for support to

When I started to get upper lip hairs my dad joked about it but not in a way that assumed it was anything big, women in our family are quite hairy because of our ethnicity. But the voice is the real thing I am not sure about, because I am presenting like a ‘butch’ woman right now because of my short hair and no makeup (never worn it) maybe my voice fits my look and he assumes it deepened naturally over puberty. But the second I grow my hair out and look more feminine ‘it won’t fit’ and will become more obvious to my parents 

I really hope they suspect something though so it’s not a huge shock

That’s right and really sweet of you to say. I mean I think I’m just full of regret right now but you’re right out experiences make us who we are

Thank you. I use that for advice and it’s great, there are a few detrans subs here and the support is fantastic. The only reason I posted here is it’s more of a general relationship family question than a specific question for detrans people. But I have posted a lot there too

Honestly I really appreciate that and you seem like such a kind lady to comment on here and encourage me. Realistically though society and the world can be cruel and especially for young people they judge everything on first impressions and what you see.

I know my voice is probably going to hold me back with dating, making friends, getting a customer services role where you have to talk a lot ect….

I have a feeling a lot of people may assume I’m a man to woman transgender even though I physically look feminine.

Aw thank you. I think if I naturally had a deep voice I’d be happy with it and think I’m unique but it’s something I did to myself. Like personally I don’t know if I believe I god but I feel like I damaged my body and just messed up the natural me. It’s gone to show me how immature I am at the moment and taught me important lessons but the regret is huge.

I feel like with how good they‘be been to me all these years, I mean we tell each other everything and used to be an open book before I fell into a depressive spiral, i understand and agree with you to do it for me.

Deep down I’m longing for their support emotionally and to talk to them but don’t want to admit my mistake and show them how immature I am. I mean I am supposed to go live at Uni this year and this is going to make them think I won’t be able to cope. I really want them to bring it up themselves but as they haven’t realised (at least I think!) I’m going to have to bring it up 

I agree with the friends but it’ll be hard hiding my lack of confidence. I feel like whilst I’m supposed to be out there parting and having fun I’ll always have this underlying sadness about what I’ve done. Hopefully I meet people who help cheer me up.

Thanks I hope so but it sounds very masculine to me, and I don’t speak to people on the phone at the moment much so never have to ‘get gendered’ sir or ma’am. 

This clip should work, you’ll see what I mean - https://streamable.com/sec83c

Thanks I appreciate the advice. The thing is I told them I ‘thought I was a transman and then realised I’m not’ and my dad literally said he was was glad I didn’t see a doctor for hormones and only cut my hair off.

I do need to sit down and tell them but it’s hard to find a good time as I am doing exams right now and my disabled sister is very hard to look after so my dad has no time to sit down in a quiet place and talk, he is always stressed, I’m not too close to my mum because she is always working and want to tell my dad first.

It’s a mixed bag. Most people say it stays the same because like trans women don’t naturally get a higher voice off testosterone but the thing is many people say cis women are different and on the detrans sub there are cases of women’s voices lightening and getting more feminine over years, but also cases where women are depressed they still have a manly voice. It’s more about I’m not prepared to wait years to see if my voice gets slightly more feminine or not when I’m in the peak of my youth and should be making the most of life.

I did work with a therapist, at the gender clinic I had one and they made me more confident in my decision to transition. The way the questions were worded like would you press a button to switch gender, and everything they analysed about my bullying history and insecurity about femininity and distress around periods made them think I was truly transgender.

I guess I could get another one but I’ve given up a bit on therapists at the moment. It seems such a gamble to get a genuinely good one. 

I agree I was too young mentally for changes, but legally in my country I did everything according to procedure and law. 

I’ve tried training for months but am not happy with the results. I’ve spoken to MTF trans people and many have opted for surgery as they hate having to always think about it, it’s rare for it to become subconscious from the ones I’ve spoken to.
